title: Mocks and contract tests
summary: Let consumers start before you finish, and prove your implementation still matches what you promised.

steps.title: Mocking from the contract
body: A contract with **examples** is enough to run a fake of the API:
- **Mock mode** in the integration itself (`missingOperation: mock`), as in lesson 2.
- Stand-alone mock servers that read OpenAPI: Prism, Microcks, WireMock (with stubs), Postman mock servers.
- **Backend stubs** in a local lab: a WireMock container standing in for the catalogue, returning fixed data
for known ISBNs, `404` for unknown ones, `500` for a magic ISBN and a long delay for another, so every
error path can be tested on a laptop.
Mocks unblock consumers and make error paths **reproducible**: you cannot ask a real backend to time out on demand.

steps.prompt: Why do stub backends usually include "magic" inputs such as an ISBN that always returns 500 or always answers slowly?
options: So every error path (502 mapping, 504 timeouts) can be tested deterministically, on demand
steps.explain: Make failure a test input. If you can only test the happy path, the error handler ships untested.

steps.title: Contract tests
body: A contract is a promise. **Contract tests** check the implementation keeps it:
- **Provider tests** (yours): call each operation and check the **status is documented** for that operation and
the **body matches the schema** for that status. An undocumented `500` or an extra `internalCost` field fails the build.
- **Consumer-driven contracts** (Pact and similar): each consumer publishes the parts of the API it actually uses;
the provider's pipeline verifies them, so you learn *before* deploying that a change breaks a real consumer.
- The gateway can also validate **responses** against the schema, but that is expensive at runtime: do it in tests.

items: `getBook` returns `500` for an unknown ISBN instead of the documented `404`
The response is missing the required `price`
The mobile app relies on `title`, which a refactoring renamed to `name`
A book is shown at the wrong price because of a tax rule
The order response returns `status: "queued"`, not in the enum

steps.prompt: Put a provider contract test run in order.
lines: Start the integration against stub backends
Call each operation with its example inputs and its magic failure inputs
Check each status code is documented for that operation
Validate each body against the schema for that status
Fail the pipeline on any difference

steps.explain: `200` for a create is a real contract break: clients may be checking for `201`.

steps.prompt: A provider contract test fails: `getBook` returned a body with an extra field `internalCost`. The schema has no `additionalProperties: false`. What should you do?
options: Treat it as a leak and remove the field in the transform; then consider `additionalProperties: false` so tests catch it automatically
Nothing: extra fields are always allowed
steps.explain: JSON Schema allows extra properties by default, so a plain schema check misses leaks. Explicitly closing response schemas in tests turns leaks into failures.

steps.title: Check a response against the contract
prompt: `Validate` (the schema validator from the previous lesson) is in your editor. Write
`List<string> CheckResponse(string openApiJson, string operationId, int status, string body)`:
- find the operation by `operationId`; none → `["unknown operation {operationId}"]`;
- status not among its `responses` → `["status {status} is not documented for {operationId}"]`;
- if that response has a JSON schema (`content.application/json.schema`), validate the parsed body against it (with the whole contract as `root`) and return the errors; otherwise return no errors.

- additionally, if the body is a JSON object, every property it has that the schema's `properties` (after resolving one `$ref`) does not list is reported as `"$.{name}: is not in the contract"`, after the validator's errors.
starter: List<string> Validate(JsonElement value, JsonElement schema, JsonElement root, string path = "$")
foreach (var part in reference.GetString()!.TrimStart('#', '/').Split('/')) target = target.GetProperty(part);
var type = schema.TryGetProperty("type", out var t) ? t.GetString() : null;
if (value.TryGetProperty(p.Name, out var child)) errors.AddRange(Validate(child, p.Value, root, $"{path}.{p.Name}"));
foreach (var item in value.EnumerateArray()) errors.AddRange(Validate(item, items, root, $"{path}[{i++}]"));
if (schema.TryGetProperty("minLength", out var minL) && s.Length < minL.GetInt32()) errors.Add($"{path}: length must be >= {minL.GetInt32()}");
if (schema.TryGetProperty("maxLength", out var maxL) && s.Length > maxL.GetInt32()) errors.Add($"{path}: length must be <= {maxL.GetInt32()}");
if (schema.TryGetProperty("pattern", out var pat) && !Regex.IsMatch(s, pat.GetString()!)) errors.Add($"{path}: does not match {pat.GetString()}");
if (schema.TryGetProperty("minimum", out var min) && d < min.GetDecimal()) errors.Add($"{path}: must be >= {min.GetDecimal()}");
if (schema.TryGetProperty("maximum", out var max) && d > max.GetDecimal()) errors.Add($"{path}: must be <= {max.GetDecimal()}");
if (schema.TryGetProperty("enum", out var allowed) && !allowed.EnumerateArray().Any(a => a.GetRawText() == value.GetRawText()))
errors.Add($"{path}: must be one of {string.Join(", ", allowed.EnumerateArray().Select(a => a.ToString()))}");

hints: Find the operation as in lesson 2, then `responses.TryGetProperty(status.ToString(), ...)`.
To list the allowed properties, resolve the `$ref` by walking from the contract root, exactly as the validator does.
template: Dojo.Eq("a good book", new List<string>(), CheckResponse(dojoContract, "getBook", 200, """{"isbn":"9780134757599","title":"Refactoring","price":44.99}"""));
Dojo.Eq("undocumented status", new List<string> { "status 500 is not documented for getBook" }, CheckResponse(dojoContract, "getBook", 500, "{}"));
Dojo.Eq("201 vs 200", new List<string> { "status 200 is not documented for createOrder" }, CheckResponse(dojoContract, "createOrder", 200, "{}"));
Dojo.Eq("missing required field and a leak", new List<string> { "$.price: is required", "$.internalCost: is not in the contract" },
Dojo.Eq("error bodies are checked too", new List<string> { "$.traceId: is required" }, CheckResponse(dojoContract, "getBook", 404, """{"code":"BOOK_NOT_FOUND"}"""));
Dojo.Eq("unknown operation", new List<string> { "unknown operation deleteBook" }, CheckResponse(dojoContract, "deleteBook", 200, "{}"));
